chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

When the thief is seized, his hand is cut from the middle of the palm. If he returns [to stealing], his foot is cut from the middle of the foot. If he returns, he is confined to prison. If he steals in prison, he is killed.
ai.seo_question: What is the progressive punishment for a repeat thief according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Sam'a ibn Mihran, a key figure in Shia hadith transmission, establishes a graduated penal system where the severity of punishment escalates with recidivism, culminating in execution for theft within prison. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on proportionality and the specific procedural detail of amputating from the 'middle of the palm' and 'middle of the foot,' distinguishing it from other schools. The final stage of execution for stealing in custody highlights the breach of security and trust inherent in the penal institution.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mahran who said,

‘When the thief is seized, cut his hand from the middle of the palm. So if he were to repeat, cut his left foot from the middle. So if he repeats, leave him in the prison. So if he steals in the prison, kill (him)’.
